title: PRD: Standard Sales Demo Environment (Demo Tenant) — v1
author: Nikhil Sharma
body:
## Summary
This PRD defines the requirements for a reliable, repeatable “Standard Demo v1” environment (“demo tenant”) used for live prospect demos and internal enablement. The demo tenant will contain a small set of known-good scenarios that consistently showcase Redwood Inference’s differentiators: production-grade performance controls (latency/cost), reliability via routing/fallback, deployment flexibility (Hosted/Dedicated/Private narrative), and first-class observability.

The environment must be safe to use live (sanitized data, controlled access), quick to reset, and resilient to common failure modes (capacity constraints, throttling confusion, output variability).

## Problem statement
Today, demo quality and reliability depend heavily on ad-hoc SE setup and “heroics.” Live demos occasionally fail due to:
- Model/version drift causing different behavior than the talk track
- Quota/rate-limit surprises (429s) and inconsistent throttling messaging
- Dashboard lag/missing panels or confusing click paths
- Routing/fallback behavior that’s hard to explain or demonstrate quickly
- Output variability causing the “same prompt” to look different between runs

These failures reduce credibility and slow down demo-to-eval conversion.

## Goals
1) Stand up a stable demo tenant that is safe and predictable for live prospect calls.
2) Provide 4–6 “known-good” demo scenarios with canned inputs, expected outputs, and plan-B fallbacks.
3) Ensure a fast, repeatable reset process (pre-demo and post-demo) with clear ownership.
4) Instrument reliability: measure scenario pass rate and demo incident rate over time.

## Non-goals
- Building a bespoke POC framework for every customer or vertical.
- Shipping major new product features beyond light demo-oriented fixes (labeling, safer defaults, docs/examples).
- Using any customer data or real customer prompts/logs in the demo tenant.

## Target users / personas
Primary:
- Platform Engineering leaders and staff engineers evaluating reliability, scaling, and deployment models
- ML/Applied AI engineers evaluating quality controls, throughput/latency, and SDK ergonomics
Secondary:
- Security/Compliance stakeholders evaluating isolation, logging, retention, and access controls
- Procurement/IT stakeholders asking about SLA posture and operational maturity

## Key user journeys
### Journey A: “2-minute Hosted mini-demo” (time-boxed)
- Run a streaming chat request via curl/SDK
- Show token streaming + basic usage telemetry (tokens, latency)
- End with a clear next step: “Try it with your prompts in an eval/trial.”

### Journey B: “Platform reliability + fallbacks” (enterprise default)
- Show a pre-configured Route with model pinning
- Demonstrate fallback policy behavior (capacity constrained / forced failure mode) without breaking the app
- Show error analysis + dashboards that prove what happened

### Journey C: “Cost/performance controls” (latency/cost proof)
- Compare a baseline config vs optimized config (batching/caching/quantization profile)
- Show before/after token cost and latency breakdown in Console

### Journey D: “Security posture (demo tenant)” (security persona)
- Explain how demo tenant is isolated, sanitized, and access-controlled
- Answer common questions: retention, encryption, SSO/RBAC options, audit logs posture, residency narrative

## Requirements
### Functional requirements (must-have)
1) Demo tenant creation and configuration
- A named, dedicated demo tenant (one per region as needed) with:
  - Model catalog entries required for scenarios
  - Route definitions for each scenario (pinning model versions + quantization profiles)
  - Routing/fallback rules for at least one scenario
  - Quotas/rate limits configured to be “demo-safe” (avoid accidental throttling during normal demo usage)
  - Prebuilt dashboards and saved views for the tenant

2) Scenario package
- 4–6 scenarios, each with:
  - Purpose (what differentiation it proves)
  - Scripted inputs (curl and at least one SDK)
  - Expected output characteristics (not necessarily byte-for-byte deterministic)
  - “What to say” notes (brief; talk track lives in Sales Enablement)
  - Plan B (if the model is slow, tool calling fails, dashboard is stale, etc.)

3) Reset and verification
- A pre-demo verification checklist and an idempotent reset mechanism to:
  - Re-apply tenant config (routes, quotas, pinned versions)
  - Re-import/verify dashboards
  - Validate scenarios via quick automated checks
- Pre-demo checks must be runnable by an SE in <10 minutes.

4) Observability for demos
- Dashboards must answer, within 30 seconds:
  - “Is the demo tenant healthy?” (error rate, saturation, latency)
  - “Did the request succeed and which route/model served it?”
  - “Was fallback triggered?”
  - “What did it cost (tokens) and what was latency breakdown?”

### Non-functional requirements
1) Reliability
- The demo tenant must be stable during business hours and resilient to common operational issues.
- Failure modes must be “graceful”:
  - If a preferred model is unavailable, fallback must serve a compatible alternative without breaking the narrative.
  - If streaming drops, provide a non-streaming variant for the same scenario.

2) Security and safety
- No customer data. Only sanitized, synthetic prompts and seed data.
- Access restricted to approved internal users (Sales/SE/PMM) with revocation path.
- Logging defaults must be “demo-safe”:
  - Avoid storing full prompts/responses beyond what is necessary to show the product (use redaction where available).
  - Include guidance for what is shown on-screen during a call.

3) Consistency / change control
- Model versions and quantization profiles must be pinned per scenario.
- Any update requires a lightweight review to avoid breaking the talk track.
- Weekly (or pre-demo) regression check to detect drift.

4) Performance
- For the “standard” scenarios, performance should be representative and consistently within published safe ranges (see “Benchmark Proof Points” inputs). Exact numbers are not shown in the deck; we show relative improvements and dashboards.

## Proposed “Known-good” scenarios (v1)
1) Streaming Chat + Developer Quickstart
- Proves: fast onboarding, streaming UX, stable baseline performance
- Assets: curl + SDK snippet; optional small UI

2) Structured Output (JSON mode) for extraction
- Proves: production-friendly outputs, reduced parsing burden
- Notes: include schema + guardrails to reduce variability

3) Tool calling (function calling) with deterministic tool stub
- Proves: agentic workflow integration, reliability of tool invocation
- Plan B: show tool calling results from recorded successful run if live tool step fails

4) Routing + fallback (graceful degradation)
- Proves: reliability differentiator; “keep the app online” story
- Implementation: route policy with a preferred model and a fallback model; ability to force fallback for the demo (flag or controlled condition)

5) Cost controls: caching/batching/quantization profile comparison
- Proves: unit economics levers + transparency in Console
- Implementation: two routes (baseline vs optimized) + dashboard view showing token cost and latency deltas

6) Observability: error analysis + traces + per-route metrics
- Proves: production operations maturity; answers “what happened” fast
- Implementation: saved dashboards + a “demo drilldown” view keyed by request_id

## Success metrics / acceptance criteria
### Primary metrics (tracked weekly)
1) Demo reliability rate (Scenario Pass Rate)
- Definition: % of scenario runs that succeed without human intervention beyond the script.
- Target: ≥ 99% pass rate for the top 4 scenarios over a rolling 30-day window.

2) Demo readiness time
- Definition: time for an SE to complete pre-demo verification on a fresh day.
- Target: ≤ 10 minutes.

3) Tenant reset time
- Definition: time to run the reset workflow and return to a known-good state.
- Target: ≤ 15 minutes end-to-end.

4) Demo incident rate
- Definition: count of P1/P2 demo-affecting incidents (dashboard missing, auth issue, scenario failing) per week.
- Target: ≤ 1 P2/month after rollout; 0 P1s.

### Secondary metrics
- Demo-to-eval conversion uplift (Sales Ops tracked; directional)
- Reduction in “SE time spent prepping demos” (self-reported + survey)
- Reduction in support tickets related to throttling confusion during trials/demos

## Rollout plan (high level)
Phase 1 — Requirements and scenario selection (Week 1)
- Finalize scenario list and persona mapping
- Confirm “safe to claim” proof points and what is shown live

Phase 2 — Demo tenant buildout (Weeks 2–4)
- Provision tenant config + pin models/versions
- Implement routing/fallback demo flow
- Create dashboards and saved views
- Add reset automation and guardrails

Phase 3 — Deck + talk track integration (Weeks 3–6)
- Ensure console click path matches the story
- Validate screenshots and any benchmark ranges are compliant

Phase 4 — Enablement and governance (Weeks 6–8)
- Train AEs/SEs
- Publish runbook + FAQ
- Establish ownership and change control

## Dependencies
### Engineering dependencies (by area)
Platform / SRE
- Demo tenant provisioning/reset automation (idempotent config; seed data) — owner: Priya Natarajan / Rafael Mendes
- Business-hours monitoring and alerting for demo tenant — owner: Sean Gallagher / Logan Wright

Control plane / Routing
- Stable routing + fallback behavior suitable for live demonstration; ability to “force fallback” safely — owner: Mina Haddad

Quotas / Rate-limits
- Demo-safe quota defaults; clear UI/message for throttling; avoid accidental 429s during standard demo load — owner: Cole Summers / Amara Diallo

Console / Observability
- Prebuilt dashboards export/import; saved views for the tenant; ensure panels are durable (no missing queries) — owner: Chloe Martin / Allison Grant

DevEx
- Scenario scripts + quickstart template; easy-to-run commands; deterministic-ish examples — owner: Renee Sullivan / Colin O'Donnell

Security
- Access control requirements; guidance on logging/redaction; alignment with security FAQ — owner: Marcus Lin / Kevin Osei / Naomi Feldman

### Go-to-market dependencies
- Standard Demo Deck v1 and talk track sign-off — owner: Soojin Lee
- Competitive objection handling alignment (what we show vs what we claim) — owner: Markus Klein / Soojin Lee

## Governance / change management
- Demo tenant changes require:
  1) PRD alignment check (does this impact scenarios/talk track?)
  2) Review from Solutions Engineering owner (Markus Klein) and relevant Eng owner (e.g., Routing, Console)
  3) Update pinned versions and re-run scenario regression checks
- Release cadence: weekly update window (Tues/Wed) with a rollback plan.

## Risks and mitigations
1) Output variability breaks narrative
- Mitigation: use prompts designed for stable behavior; validate “expected output characteristics” rather than exact text; keep canned screenshots/recorded output as plan B.

2) Quota/rate limit surprises during a live call
- Mitigation: demo-safe quotas; pre-demo checklist; dedicated keys; clear guidance for interpreting 429s.

3) Dashboard drift or missing panels
- Mitigation: versioned dashboard exports; import tests in reset workflow; keep a minimal “health view” separate from complex panels.

4) Model availability / capacity constraints
- Mitigation: pinned primary + fallback model; ability to run non-streaming variant; business-hours alerting.

5) Access/login issues block the demo
- Mitigation: documented access request + revocation; backup credentials procedure (restricted); pre-demo auth check.

## Open questions
1) Regions: do we need an EU-only demo tenant for EMEA data residency conversations, or is narrative-only sufficient for v1?
2) “Force fallback” mechanism: do we prefer a dedicated toggle in the route policy, a synthetic failure injection header, or a scheduled capacity constraint window?
3) Retention/logging posture: what default retention window is safest for the demo tenant while still enabling meaningful observability screens?
4) Who owns “demo incident triage” during business hours (SE on duty vs platform on-call), and what is the escalation threshold?

## Appendix: Definition of Done (v1)
- Demo tenant exists and can be reset idempotently.
- At least 4 scenarios meet ≥ 99% pass rate in internal dry runs across 2 weeks.
- Pre-demo verification is documented and consistently <10 minutes.
- Dashboards and click paths are stable and match the deck.
- Security FAQ aligns with actual demo tenant settings and is reviewed by Security.
- Ownership and change governance are documented, including update cadence and rollback steps.
